Dear Acceleron Shareholders,
I am pleased to report that as we execute on our priorities for 2021 and beyond, Acceleron’s
fundamentals have never been stronger. In 2020, the reporting of strong results from clinical trials of
sotatercept and the successful commercial launch of REBLOZYL® (luspatercept-aamt) helped position
Acceleron for long-term growth as a leader in rare pulmonary and hematologic diseases. Even against
the backdrop of the global pandemic, we were able to make significant progress in all of our programs.
Perhaps most importantly, our team of Accelerators remains steadfastly committed to our mission to
transform the lives of patients with serious and rare diseases.
Sotatercept, our lead pulmonary asset, is an investigation al reverse-remodeling agent with the
potential to alter the treatment paradigm for patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).
The January 2020 release of positive topline results from the PULSAR Phase 2 trial established proof-ofconcept for sotatercept in PAH while also triggering a number of important milestones in its
development, including:
(cid:120) Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA),
(cid:120) Priority Medicine (PRIME) designation from the European Medicines Agency (EMA),
(cid:120) An oral presentation in the “Breaking News” session at the American Thoracic Society 2020
Conference, and
(cid:120) The “Cardiopulmonary Best Abstract” award at the American Heart Association 2020 Scientific
Sessions.
Adding to this illustrious list of accomplishments, the editors of the New England Journal of Medicine—
one of the world’s most prestigious peer-reviewed medical journals—selected the PULSAR trial results
for publication in the April 1, 2021 issue.
The PULSAR trial produced a concordance of clinically meaningful results across multiple study
endpoints in patients receiving mono, double, and triple PAH-specific therapies. Sotatercept was
generally well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with that observed in other patient populations.
Acceleron’s clinical development plan is designed to support our long-term vision to establish
sotatercept as a backbone therapy for patients with PAH at all stages of disease. We initiated the
registrational STELLAR Phase 3 trial in a PAH patient population similar to the PULSAR trial late last year.
We plan to have the HYPERION and ZENITH Phase 3 trials, evaluating sotatercept in newly diagnosed
patients and in patients diagnosed with World Health Organization (WHO) functional class IV disease,
respectively, initiated by the second half of this

3 trial in a PAH patient population similar to the PULSAR trial late last year.
We plan to have the HYPERION and ZENITH Phase 3 trials, evaluating sotatercept in newly diagnosed
patients and in patients diagnosed with World Health Organization (WHO) functional class IV disease,
respectively, initiated by the second half of this year.
In parallel to planning our Phase 3 trials in PAH, our research and development team has been
evaluating sotatercept in patients with pulmonary hypertension. Following positive preclinical proof-ofconcept studies, we plan to initiate a clinical trial evaluating sotatercept in a population of patients with
pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease (PH-LHD) before the end of this year. If successful, we
believe that sotatercept has the potential to be an important medicine for these patients for whom
there are no currently approved medicines.
We are also advancing a second pulmonary asset, ACE-1334, into a Phase 1b/Phase 2 trial in patients
with systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD), a rare connective tissue disorder

and the leading cause of death among patients with systemic scleroderma. We expect to start this trial
later this year.
In light of the progress we’re making in advancing our pipeline, we look forward to hosting a mid-year
research and development day which will primarily focus on providing additional details of the
sotatercept and ACE-1334 programs, and highlight our long-term strategic vision for the treatment of
rare pulmonary diseases of high unmet medical needs.
In hematology, we and our partner Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) estimate annual peak sales of
REBLOZYL in excess of $4 billion, assuming success in existing and potential future anemia indications.
BMS achieved multiple regulatory milestones during REBLOZYL’s first full year of commercial availability
in the United States, including approval in a second indication and ongoing global market expansion.
REBLOZYL is the first and only erythroid maturation agent approved in the United States, Europe, and
Canada, for the treatment of anemia in certain adult patient populations of myelodysplastic syndromes
and beta-thalassemia.
2020 was a successful first year for REBLOZYL, as our partner BMS reported approximately $274 million
in net sales of REBLOZYL for the year. Despite the many external challenges imposed by the global
pandemic, our joint commercial team was able to drive early sales success through

adult patient populations of myelodysplastic syndromes
and beta-thalassemia.
2020 was a successful first year for REBLOZYL, as our partner BMS reported approximately $274 million
in net sales of REBLOZYL for the year. Despite the many external challenges imposed by the global
pandemic, our joint commercial team was able to drive early sales success through virtual engagement
and education. We benefited from significant awareness in the scientific community from the 2018
American Society of Hematology (ASH) Plenary Session presentation and the New England Journal of
Medicine publications of the Phase 3 trial results in early 2020. Importantly, physician feedback remains
positive through the early stages of the launch.
Outside of the U.S., BMS launched REBLOZYL in Austria and Germany late last year, and we anticipate
launches in additional markets globally as reimbursements are approved throughout the course of 2021.
As we consider long-term growth of the brand, our partner BMS continues to advance the development
of REBLOZYL for the treatment of additional patient populations struggling with anemia-associated
blood disorders. Three trials are currently underway to investigate luspatercept’s potential in patients
with first-line lower-risk MDS (the COMMANDS trial), non-transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia (the
BEYOND trial), and myelofibrosis (the INDEPENDENCE trial). The joint development teams remain
focused on evaluating additional opportunities as part of a robust life-cycle management plan for
REBLOZYL.
At Acceleron, we believe that our future success depends on our ability to attract, motivate, and
retain the best possible employees. Accordingly, over the past year, we have invested meaningfully in
strategies to support and engage our talented workforce.
We have long celebrated diversity, and our team of more than 325 strong includes Accelerators with an
impressive breadth of backgrounds, skills, and interests. Global events throughout the past year have
taught us the importance of tackling issues of equity, diversity, and inclusion head on, and we have
worked diligently to embrace operations and initiatives that promote a safe work environment, provide
equal employment opportunities, and support the communities in which we work and live.

As we advance the organization through this year and beyond, we do so from a position of operational
and fiscal strength, holding nearly $860 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments as of the end
of 2020. Our commitment to long-term growth initiatives remains resolute as we continue

which we work and live.

As we advance the organization through this year and beyond, we do so from a position of operational
and fiscal strength, holding nearly $860 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments as of the end
of 2020. Our commitment to long-term growth initiatives remains resolute as we continue to take a
strategic, disciplined approach to investing, be it in our internal programs or external business
development opportunities.
In conclusion, I would like to thank the patients, families, and caregivers who have participated in our
trials and supported our research. We are humbled by these brave and passionate individuals who
remind us daily why we do what we do. I would also like to extend my gratitude to our partners,
employees, and investors for their continued commitment to Acceleron. Owing to the contributions of
so many, we were able to emerge from a particularly challenging year poised to deliver for patients in
need.
Sincerely,
Habib Dable
President and Chief Executive Officer
Acceleron Pharma Inc.
